topic: Sultan Abdul Hamid II — the last day of his reign (27 April 1909)
facts: Acceded 31 August 1876 after Murad V was deposed; reigned until 27 April 1909 (~33 years).
Parliament under the 1876 constitution was suspended in 1878 and only restored in July 1908 (~30 years).
Losses during his reign: Cyprus to Britain (1878), Egypt under de facto British control (1882), Balkan states independent/autonomous after 1878 (Congress of Berlin).
Refused Herzl's 1896 offer to pay down Ottoman debt in exchange for Palestine; quoted as saying he would not sell even a foot of the land.
Young Turk Revolution, July 1908: troops in Salonica; constitution restored 24 July 1908.
31 March Incident: uprising in Constantinople on 13 April 1909 against the CUP.
Action Army (Hareket Ordusu) came from Salonica by train, entered Constantinople on 24 April 1909.
27 April 1909: General National Assembly met behind closed doors, fatwa read, voted to depose him; Mehmed V proclaimed.
Four delegates (Esad Pasha Toptani, Emmanuel Karasu, Arif Hikmet Pasha, Aram Efendi) informed him; Esad: 'the nation has deposed you'.
Taken into captivity at Salonica (Villa Allatini); returned to Constantinople 1912; died at Beylerbeyi Palace in 1918.
